## Summary

v8 should plan tension and energy as two separate curves before writing any notes. Harmonic tension should build in the pre-chorus and bridge and resolve on the chorus's first bar; energy should peak in the chorus. Both should come late in the song, and the chord, melody and band writers should be gated by measured targets. v7 has no such plan, and its one harmony measure (a 1-to-3 number per chord) predicts nothing.

- **The research record.** Every tension model that fits listeners reads trends, not levels. It gives harmony a long memory (about 20 seconds) and pitch, loudness and density short ones (2 to 4 seconds). Listeners track tension mostly from cadence to cadence, not across the whole song's tonal plan.

- **Structure.** Full structural analysis by computer is still unreliable, and listeners hear only a level or two. The engine needs phrase goals and section goals, which it already knows because it writes its own chords.

- **Pop theory.** Each verse, pre-chorus and chorus cycle builds to an arrival. Melody and harmony build a "syntactic" climax; texture, register and loudness build a "statistical" one. The late breakdown and rebuild that soul and gospel gave pop sits at about 0.62 and 0.80 of the song.

- **Measured here, on 214 charting songs (100 rated by listeners):**

   - Harmonic tension is highest in the pre-chorus (+0.54 standard deviations) and bridge (+0.37), with the dominant just before each chorus (+0.51) and the tonic on its first bar (+0.43). Arousal peaks in the chorus.

   - Harmonic tension peaks at about 0.68 of the song, energy at about 0.74.

   - Per bar, harmony says almost nothing about arousal; given a long memory, it adds a little. Melodic height is the score's best signal, and loudness does better still.

- **The engine's songs 54 and 55.** Both put the dominant before every chorus. Song 54 never lands a chorus on the tonic and puts its harmonic tension in the choruses, the reverse of kept songs.

## What Luthier v7 does with tension now

v7 uses the word tension on almost every page, but it measures tension in four crude ways and never plans it before the notes exist. Read from the spec (15,350 lines) and the engine of record ( `songs/p66/melody_l7_p66.py` ).

|Item|Where in v7|What it does|Its limit|
|---|---|---|---|
|Tension timeline|Module 8|Scores rendered audio with the TenseMusic weights (Barchet et al. 2024): loudness 0.25, pitch height 0.20, tonal tension 0.20, roughness 0.15, tempo change 0.10, onsets 0.10; flags a peak outside the bridge|Runs only after the song is written and rendered; nothing writes toward it|
|A chord's tension|Table CO, 27.29|A hand number per chord: V and vii° 3, IV and ii 2, vi and iii 1; Lerdahl's distance from the tonic printed beside it|One number per chord, blind to what came before, to the melody, to the key's deeper plan|
|The hook at maximum tension|Windows 17, 42, 45; 27.4|The hook was to land where the chord is most tense|Window 42: the title's word sits at the chorus's most tense chord in only 27% of hits, and listeners' arousal rises at peak notes (p 0.0021) but not at the most tense bars (p 0.77). Window 45: harmonic tension is the weakest leg (nothing in choruses)|
|Structural tones|Module 7|Rewards structural tones reached by step, and a stepwise fall across the sections' high points (the Urlinie flag)|The only notion of deeper structure; which notes are structural is decided by simple rules|
|Surprise|Window 46; 749.18|Melody and chord surprise from a variable- order model|Window 46 found no arousal signal from it (coefficient 0.092, p 0.46)|
|Intensity curve|749.17 (proposed)|A per-bar curve from melodic height, singing, texture and dynamics, peaking at 0.65 to 0.85 of the song|Leaves out harmony and expectation, the two things tonal tension is made of|
|Departure budgets|Parts VII to IX; Module 2|Hand-set costs for each departure, by song type|A budget, not a curve: it says how much, not where tension rises and falls|

The gap, in one line: nothing models how tension builds and resolves through a phrase from the chords and the melody together, nothing tests such a curve against listeners, and nothing writes toward one. The weak listener result in Windows 42 and 45 tested the engine's 1-to-3 chord number, not tension as the research models it, so it may say more about the measure than about tension.

## The academic record: models of tension tested against listeners

Four decades of listening experiments agree on three things v7 does not do. Tension is heard as a trend, not a level. Harmony works on a long clock (about 20 seconds) while loudness, pitch and note density work on short ones (2 to 4 seconds). And listeners track tension locally, cadence to cadence, more than through the whole song's tonal plan.

|Model|What it reads|Tested on|Fit to listeners|
|---|---|---|---|
|[Lerdahl's tonal tension model](https://core.ac.uk/download/337616552.pdf) (Lerdahl 1996, 2001; Lerdahl and Krumhansl 2007)|Four parts: a tree of which events are structural, distance in tonal pitch space, surface dissonance (the top note's degree, inversion), and melodic attraction|Classical passages; continuous and stop- tension ratings|Average adjusted R² about .72 against listeners, as summarised by Ruiz- Marcos, Willis and Laney (2020); the hierarchical part matters, the attraction part has not been supported ( [Farbood and Upham 2013](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3874841))|
|[Farbood's parametric, temporal model](https://bpb-us-e1.wpmucdn.com/wp.nyu.edu/dist/f/11865/files/2020/08/Farbood_2012_Musical_Tension.pdf) (2012)|Slopes of pitch height and loudness (weight 3), tempo and onset rate (2), harmony from Lerdahl's model and the bass's and inner lines' height (1), over 3-second windows; a trend that continues is amplified|2,661 web listeners; 33 in the lab with a slider; 10 excerpts|r .67 to .99; models of feature levels predicted poorly and overfit; melodic expectation was dropped for lack of a clear direction|
|[Farbood and Upham](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3874841) (2013)|The same model, with each feature's window fitted|A Schubert song and its harmonic reduction, 25 listeners|Harmony's best window 21.5 s against 2 to 4 s for the rest; harmony correlated best with mean tension (ρ.58), loudness .52;ρ.79 on held-out verses|
|[Spiral-array tension](https://core.ac.uk/download/77040497.pdf) (Herremans and Chew 2016)|Spread of the notes in tonal space, movement of their centre, and distance from the key|Compared by eye with Farbood's web data|Agreement 30% to 60%; no melody, register or inversion; it drives [MorpheuS,](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1812.04832v1.pdf) which rewrites a piece to a given tension profile|
|[Tonal Interval Space model](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7712964) (Navarro- Cáceres et al. 2020)|Dissonance, a tree from Rohrmeier's harmonic grammar, distance from the key, voice leading|15 trained listeners, 12 progressions|r .75 (R² .56), against .64 to .68 for Lerdahl's refitted; weights dissonance .40, hierarchy .25, distance .20, voice leading .19|
|[TenseMusic](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10798497/) (Barchet et al. 2024; v7's Module 8)|Six audio features, a weighted sum of slopes, fitted by Lasso|38 classical pieces|Held-out r about .60|
|[IDyOM melodic expectation](https://escholarship.mcgill.ca/downloads/7h149t925) (Gingras et al. 2016)|Note-by-note surprise and uncertainty|A Couperin prelude, 12 performances, 50 listeners|Modest: model r .54 to .65 by group, and it added nothing once performance timing was included|

What the experiments add beyond the models:

- **Trends, not levels.** In Farbood's web study, a feature mattered when it moved in a clear direction; in her words, a clear trend "generated the expectancy that the trend would continue".

- **Local before global.** Bigand and Parncutt (1999) found tension in long chord sequences [mainly set locally by cadences,](https://lead.ube.fr/publications/perceiving-musical-tension-in-long-chord-sequences/) heard through a short window sliding from cadence to cadence; the hierarchical model fit best only because it caught those local cadences. Farbood (2016) found listeners' [memory of a home key fades](https://bpb-us-e1.wpmucdn.com/wp.nyu.edu/dist/f/11865/files/2020/08/Farbood_MP_2016_Memory_after_Modulation.pdf) within tens of seconds in a new key.

- **Which layers carry it.** In [Lehne et al. (2013)](https://stefan-koelsch.de/papers/Lehne_MP120731_tension_music.pdf), the outer voices alone kept most of the tension curve (ρ .71 and .73 with the original), and removing dynamics kept its shape (.83, .71). Melody or harmony led depending on the piece: melody where the harmony changed slowly.

- **Parameters interact.** [Granot and Eitan (2011)](https://cris.iucc.ac.il/en/publications/musical-tension-and-the-interaction-of-dynamic-auditory-parameter/), 132 listeners: loudness change, pitch direction and register each raised tension and tempo did not, with strong interactions between them, so fixed weights are an approximation.

- **Tension is not arousal.** [Lehne and Koelsch (2015)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4324075) define tension as conflict, instability, dissonance or uncertainty that sets up a prediction of something significant; high tension always brings high arousal, but not the reverse. Huron's tension response is likewise uncertainty felt as stress before an event ([Sweet Anticipation](https://ci.nii.ac.jp/ncid/BA90886160?l=en)).

- **Expectation and pleasure.** [Cheung et al. (2019)](https://cms.mus.cam.ac.uk/publications/cheung-uncertainty-surprise/) found, on Billboard chords, pleasure where a surprise follows low uncertainty, or where an uncertain moment resolves as expected. v7 already carries this as 749.18.

- **Builds in dance-pop.** In [Turrell et al. (2025)](https://kar.kent.ac.uk/106400/2/Building%20the%20anticipation_Javadi_AAM.pdf), felt tension rose almost linearly through EDM build-ups (ρ .998), peaked at the drop and fell 2 to 3 seconds after; tension tracked arousal (ρ .92) and ran against valence (−.69).

This explains Windows 42 and 45. They read one fixed number per chord as a level, bar by bar, against arousal. Every model that fits listeners reads slopes, gives harmony a long memory, and treats arousal as related to tension but not the same.

## Structure: which notes are structural

Full structural analysis by computer is still unreliable, and listeners mostly hear structure one or two levels deep. So v8 should model a shallow hierarchy (phrase goals and section goals), not a full Schenkerian or GTTM tree.

|Approach|What it builds|How well it works|
|---|---|---|
|GTTM (Lerdahl and|Grouping, metre, a time-span|The latest, [deepGTTM-IV](https://zenodo.org/records/10114163),|
|Jackendoff 1983) and its|tree and a prolongation tree:|got the right time-span tree|
|programs: ATTA, FATTA,|which note each note|for 29 of 30 test pieces;|
|σGTTM and deepGTTM|elaborates|Ruiz-Marcos et al.'s|
|(Hamanaka, Hirata and Tojo,||automatic tension program|
|2005 onward)||reached only .33 tree accuracy ( [2020)](https://core.ac.uk/download/337616552.pdf)|
|Learned Schenkerian analysis ( [Kirlin and Jensen 2015)](https://www.cs.rhodes.edu/~kirlinp/papers/kirlin15using.pdf)|The most probable tree of prolongations for a melody, learned from 41 textbook analyses|64% of links right with no hints, 90% when told the background notes, 22% by chance; experts graded textbook analyses half a grade to a grade higher|
|What decides a structural note ( [Kirlin and Yust 2015](https://people.bu.edu/jyust/jmm-nov15.pdf))|Removes features one at a time from that model|Melodic features matter most (interval pattern, then scale degree); harmony is the best single feature and lifts accuracy from about 52% to 60%; metric strength next; chord tone or not is nearly useless alone|
|Proto-voices ( [Finkensiep and Rohrmeier 2021)](https://zenodo.org/record/5624431)|Neighbour and passing notes and arpeggiations built up recursively, with no fixed voices|A grammar and a chart parser for free textures, a base for schemata and harmonies|
|Harmonic grammars (Rohrmeier 2011; [Harasim, Rohrmeier and O'Donnell 2018;](https://ismir2018.ismir.net/doc/pdfs/258_Paper.pdf) [2019](https://zenodo.org/records/3527812/files/ismir2019_paper_000039.pdf))|Trees of chord dependencies (prolongation and preparation); a version with rhythm|Parses jazz; adding harmonic rhythm improves the grammar; used for the hierarchical term in the Tonal Interval Space model above|

### What pop theory adds:

- **Melody and harmony can run on separate frameworks.** Temperley (2007) found rock's unresolved non-chord tones come [mostly in pentatonic melodies and in verses](https://www.icce.rug.nl/~soundscapes/BEAB/abstracts/beab0490.shtml), with choruses tightening melody to harmony ("loose verse, tight chorus"). [Nobile (2015)](https://mtosmt.org/docs/diss-index.php?id=460) names three kinds of divorce (hierarchy, loop and syntax), and [de Clercq (2019)](https://www.midside.com/publications/declercq_2019_spectrum.pdf) finds the same independence between harmony and bass. So in pop the structural line may live in the melody alone, over a loop.

- **The chorus closes.** Nobile's _Form as Harmony in Rock Music_ (2020, already in v7's citations) treats the chorus as the section that brings harmonic closure; Biamonte notes that pop phrases often end without a cadence, their momentum [pointing to the next unit](https://music.arts.uci.edu/abauer/6.2/readings/Routledge_Companion_Popular_Music_Analysis__Biamonte_rhythmic_fctns-13_chapter.pdf).

For the engine, three consequences. Module 7's rule (structural tones on strong beats, reached by step) is the right instinct but weighs the wrong things: melodic interval pattern and harmony matter more than metric weight, and chord-tone status alone says almost nothing. The deeper level the engine needs is two goals: each phrase's arrival note and chord, and each section's. And a tight chorus over a loose verse is itself a tension move the engine can make.

## Tension in popular song

Pop theory describes tension as two kinds working together: a syntactic build in the chords and melody toward a goal, and a statistical build in texture, register, loudness and rhythm. Each verse, pre-chorus and chorus repeats the cycle, and the song's largest build comes late.

- **Two kinds of climax.** Carter (2025), after Meyer, separates them: melody, rhythm and harmony build toward a [syntactic climax](https://theory.esm.rochester.edu/integral/?p=9827), while timbre, texture, register and dynamics build toward a statistical one. In v8 terms the first belongs to the chord and melody writers, the second to the band writer.

- **The cycle has a goal.** [Nobile (2022)](https://mtosmt.org/ojs/index.php/mto/article/view/864/206) calls it the telos principle: the verse initiates (holding tonic), the pre-chorus builds (moving to IV, ii or vi and ending on V, its phrases shrinking to one or two bars, its texture thickening), and the chorus arrives, its first downbeat the structural cadence. After 1991 texture, timbre and vocal delivery could carry the build over a single loop; after 2010 songs stretch the build, make the chorus the quietest point (the anti-telos chorus), or move the release to a drop. [Summach (2011)](https://mtosmt.org/issues/mto.11.17.3/mto.11.17.3.summach.php) traces the pre-chorus to the 'd' phrase of srdc, whose job is momentum.

- **Rhythm and drums build too.** [Biamonte](https://music.arts.uci.edu/abauer/6.2/readings/Routledge_Companion_Popular_Music_Analysis__Biamonte_rhythmic_fctns-13_chapter.pdf): verses are looser, choruses tighter and thicker; a pre-chorus can drop the drums to half time so the chorus backbeat lands harder; denser fills at section ends act as pickups; a shortened bar at a phrase end drives forward. Fink (2011) shows the same goal-directed rhythm in late-1960s Motown soul [(JAMS)](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-society-for-american-music/article/abs/new-riffs-on-the-old-mindbody-blues-black-rhythm-white-logic-and-music-theory-in-the-twentyfirst-century/BAA49A571C6D1F4A3E95F4173D9BBC8B).

- **Builds at the start.** Attas (2015) on the buildup introduction, which adds layers to an arrival; Spicer (2004) on accumulative form (both via [Biamonte's references)](https://music.arts.uci.edu/abauer/6.2/readings/Routledge_Companion_Popular_Music_Analysis__Biamonte_rhythmic_fctns-13_chapter.pdf).

- **The late rebuild.** Carter's 118 songs (1959 to 2024) break down to almost nothing at a median 62.6% of the song and arrive back at full strength at 79.9%, a median 33 seconds later, usually in three stages of four bars, usually into the chorus. Texture and density build in steps, dynamics and timbre smoothly. He traces it to gospel and soul

("What'd I Say", "Shout", both 1959) and estimates up to one pop or rock song in eight uses it. These are the places v7's own findings 749.19 (a breath at 0.55 to 0.60) and 749.17 (a high point at 0.65 to 0.85) already name, now with a mechanism.

- **The ending as climax.** [Osborn (2013):](https://kuscholarworks.ku.edu/entities/publication/3d577385-1583-4411-ba38-59a7e3a734f4) in terminally climactic forms, common in rock after 1990, the real high point is new material heard once at the end, beyond the chorus.

- **Builds and drops measured.** In EDM, felt tension rises almost linearly through the build and peaks at the drop ([Turrell et al. 2025)](https://kar.kent.ac.uk/106400/2/Building%20the%20anticipation_Javadi_AAM.pdf); drops brought higher skin conductance than the rest of the break routine [(Solberg and Dibben 2019](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/145911/)).

- **Tension as its own dimension.** Temperley's _The Musical Language of Rock_ (2018) models expression in three dimensions, valence, energy and tension, and traces shifts in them within songs ([publisher's summary](https://www.abebooks.fr/9780190653774/Musical-Language-Rock-Temperley-0190653779/plp)). Energy (v7's intensity) and tension are not the same axis.

For Jason's songs this matters directly. Soul and gospel are where the breakdown and rebuild come from, and Fink's case is Motown. Song 56's soul ballad is exactly the kind of song whose tension plan v8 must write, not leave to a hand arrangement.

## Measured here: tension readings on real songs and the engine's

Harmonic tension and the listeners' felt energy are two different curves in real hits: harmonic tension peaks in the pre-chorus and the bridge and resolves on the chorus's first bar, while arousal peaks in the chorus itself. Neither the engine's 1-to-3 chord value nor any per-bar harmony reading predicts arousal, which is why Windows 42 and 45 found nothing.

![Harmonic tension peaks before the chorus; arousal peaks in it](data:image/png;base64,)

*CoCoPops Billboard (Condit-Schultz, Arthur et al.; CC BY-NC 4.0): studies/tension/section_results.json*

**The data.** CoCoPops Billboard [(GitHub)](https://github.com/Computational-Cognitive-Musicology-Lab/CoCoPops): 214 charting songs from 1959 to 1991 with expert melody and chord transcriptions, 100 of them with four listeners' continuous arousal and valence and the recording's loudness. Each bar got Lerdahl's chord distance from the tonic and from the previous chord (it reproduces Table CO's values: V and IV 5, vi and iii 7, ii and vii° 8), the engine's old chord value, chord dissonance, melodic height and highest note, onsets per second, how much of the bar is sung, and the share of sung time on nonchord tones.

**Models against listeners** (100 songs, 10,289 rated bars; R² on held-out songs, arousal taken within song, each feature given a memory of its own length):

|Reading|Best memory|R², held-out songs|
|---|---|---|
|Engine's old chord value|32 s|0.009|
|Lerdahl distance from the tonic|32 s (0.000 with none)|0.017|
|Melody and texture|8 s|0.060|
|Everything in the score|harmony 32 s, the rest 8 s|0.066|
|The recording's loudness|8 s|0.084|
|Score and loudness|harmony 32 s, the rest 8 s|0.126|

### What the numbers say:

- **The ceiling is low.** Two halves of the listeners agree at a median of .49 (corrected; quartiles .10 and .77), so no model can reach far.

- **Melody height is the score's best signal.** It correlates .14 with arousal within songs (positive in 68% of songs); the highest note .13. Loudness does more (median song r .20).

- **Harmony works only on a long clock.** Per bar it correlates about .03 with arousal. Given a memory, its value keeps rising out to 48 seconds, the same long harmonic window Farbood and Upham found in a Schubert song.

- **Harmony carries the syntactic build.** At the last bar before a chorus the dominant is 0.51 standard deviations above its song's mean; on the chorus's first bar the tonic is 0.43 above, harmonic distance falls (−0.22) and the melody jumps (+0.38). The arousal ratings lag behind this by a bar or two.

- **Both builds come late.** Smoothed harmonic tension peaks at a median 0.68 of the song (quartiles 0.48 and 0.86), a little before melodic height (0.75), loudness (0.73) and arousal (0.74), as a bridge or rebuild comes before the last chorus.

**The engine's songs 54 and 55** (country, no pre-chorus or bridge; chords typed by an AI, melody by the engine). Both put the dominant in the last bar before every chorus. Song 54 starts none of its four choruses on the tonic and carries its highest harmonic tension in the choruses (+0.54), where kept songs keep the chorus near the song's mean (+0.05) and build in the pre-chorus. Song 55's tension peaks at 0.93 of the song. The engine's melodies already lift strongly at the chorus (+1.25 and +1.41 at bar 1, against +0.38 in kept songs). Two songs show only what a tension reader would flag, not a rate.

Cautions: arousal is not tension, the ratings are of 1959 to 1991 hits, and Lerdahl's distance here has no tree above the phrase. The result is clear enough to build on: plan harmonic tension and energy as two curves, and give harmony a long memory.

## What this means for v8: a tension plan the writers follow

v8 should plan two curves before any notes are written, harmonic tension and energy, and have the chord, melody and band writers draw toward them, with the measured targets below as gates. Because the engine writes its own chords, it already knows where its cadences fall; it does not need to parse a tree.

1. **The tension reader (score only).**

   - _Harmonic tension:_ Lerdahl's distance from the tonic and from the last chord, plus chord dissonance, with a long memory (about 30 seconds), and two levels of goal: each phrase's arrival chord and each section's.

   - _Energy:_ melodic height and onset rate with an 8-second memory, plus the band's parts playing and dynamics from the band writer (749.17's curve). _Expectation:_ 749.18's surprise and uncertainty, unchanged.

2. **The plan, per song type, drawn from kept songs.**

   - Pre-chorus: harmonic tension about half a standard deviation above the song's mean, moving off the tonic and ending on V (in kept songs the dominant is +0.51 at the last bar before a chorus).

   - Chorus: lands on the tonic at bar 1 (+0.43) with a melodic jump (+0.38); its harmonic tension near the song's mean; the energy high. The chorus resolves; it is not the tense part.

   - Bridge: the second harmonic build (+0.37), its smoothed peak at about 0.68 of the song (quartiles 0.48 to 0.86), just before the energy peak at about 0.74.

   - Optional rebuild (soul, gospel, rock ballads): thin to almost nothing at about 0.62, rebuild in about three four-bar stages, arrive at about 0.80 on the chorus (Carter 2025). This is the mechanism behind 749.19 and 749.17.

   - Verse looser than chorus: more melody off the chord tones in the verse, tighter in the chorus (Temperley 2007).

3. **How each writer uses it.** The chord writer (from the harmony study) draws section progressions and keeps those whose harmonic-tension profile fits the plan. The melody search keeps aiming at chord tones and adds the chorus-bar-1 lift. The band writer (from the arrangement study) builds the energy curve: half-time pre-chorus drums, fills as pickups into sections, the rebuild's terraced entries.

4. **The hook lands on the release.** In kept hits the title's word sits over the tonic (37%) more often than over the chorus's most tense chord (27%), and listeners' arousal rises at peak notes, not at the most tense bars (Window 42). The convergence rule's "maximum harmonic tension" leg should be restated as "the resolution after the build".

5. **What to retire or restate.** The 1-to-3 chord value (Table CO) is retired; it predicts nothing. Module 8's audio scorer stays as an after-the-fact check, not the plan. Module 7's structural-tone rule is reweighted toward melodic interval pattern and harmony, and chord-tone status alone is dropped (Kirlin and Yust 2015).

**Tests.** (a) On held-out kept songs the reader reproduces the section profile (pre-chorus above verse, V before the chorus, I and a lift at chorus bar 1, peak at 0.5 to 0.9); (b) every v8 song passes its type's tension plan or says why not; (c) the no-hand-input test: the plan comes from the intake answers, not from typing; (d) a listening check of plan against no plan on the same lyric.

**Still open.** No open dataset of continuous _tension_ ratings on pop songs turned up; the closest are CoCoPops' arousal ratings and EDM build clips. A small listening study rating tension on 20 to 30 of the engine's songs and kept songs would settle the weights. MorpheuS (Herremans and Chew), which rewrites music to a given tension profile, is a working precedent if the draw-and-gate approach falls short.
